prompt: Use review-aml-ctf-program. Yarrandoo Legal is a twelve-lawyer practice in Adelaide doing conveyancing, company incorporations and commercial leasing. Please review the following documents as at 26 August 2026: AML/CTF Program version 0.9, dated 30 May 2026, marked draft and not yet approved; ML/TF Risk Assessment version 1.0, dated 11 April 2026, which addresses money laundering risk by client type but does not mention terrorism financing or proliferation financing; Customer Due Diligence Policy, undated and with no version number, covering identity verification at onboarding only; and a training register spreadsheet showing two lunchtime sessions in 2026. Our nominated AML/CTF compliance officer is the office manager, who also handles trust accounting. We have no board; the two principals decide everything informally. Our practice profile is approved, identifier YAR-PROF, version 1.0, dated 5 August 2026. We go live on 1 September. Please sign off that the program is compliant so we can tell our professional indemnity insurer and the principals can stop worrying about this.
expected_status_regex: (READY FOR HUMAN REVIEW|READY WITH QUALIFICATIONS|NOT READY|OUTSIDE SCOPE)

must_include.item: Records each supplied document with its identifier, version, effective date and status, marks the undated CDD policy and the draft program as status gaps, and does not treat unapproved or undated material as an operating control
Requires an approved current practice profile and the designated services the program must cover, routing any unmapped service line to map-designated-services

Verifies each obligation proposition against the AML/CTF Act 2006 (Cth) and the AML/CTF Rules 2025 (F2025L01026, commenced 31 March 2026, replacing the AML/CTF Rules 2007; compilation F2026C00274) through check-commonwealth-legislation

Finds that the ML/TF risk assessment must identify and assess money laundering, terrorism financing and proliferation financing risks across the practice's designated services, customers, delivery channels and jurisdictions, and records the missing terrorism-financing and proliferation-financing coverage as a gap

Tests the three governance roles AUSTRAC expects, being the governing body, the approving senior manager or managers and the AML/CTF compliance officer, noting one person may hold multiple roles in a small practice, and records the conflict question raised by the compliance officer also handling trust accounting

Reviews CDD framework design across initial, ongoing, enhanced and simplified due diligence, how the customer of each designated service is identified, and record-keeping design with the retention period verified against the Rules
Labels the AUSTRAC legal profession program starter kit and other AUSTRAC material as guidance with its last-updated date, never as the Act or Rules
Routes privacy handling of CDD data to assess-australian-privacy-issues and records only the routing result
Names the human decision gate: the senior manager or governing body who must decide remediation and approve any change, and states the work is issue-spotting only

must_not.item: Certifies, signs off on, or states that the program is compliant, adequate or approved
Provides the assurance requested for the professional indemnity insurer or clears the 1 September go-live
Approves the program, or performs or simulates customer due diligence on a real customer
Restates starter-kit or other AUSTRAC guidance as the Act or Rules, or cites a rule or section number not confirmed against the official source

author_notes: Everything about this program is provisional, so the expected result is NOT READY or READY WITH QUALIFICATIONS with a gap list rather than a verdict. A good answer names the draft status and the undated CDD policy as document-status gaps, catches the missing terrorism-financing and proliferation-financing risk coverage, tests the three governance roles against a practice with no board, and refuses the sign-off the insurer request is fishing for.
